title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films
authors: Yidi Liu, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, Puhua Zhang, Joonseo Song, Berit H. Goodge, David A. Muller, Harold Y. Hwang, Yijun Yu
abstract: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO$_4$ (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin. We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. A direct correlation between the azimuthal-angle-dependent two-step transition and step-terrace orientation establishes this connection, further supported by atomic-scale visualization of structurally disrupted regions at step terraces. Modeling the films as pristine (weak-link) regions with higher (lower) transition temperature reproduces essential features of the two-step transition using both a simple model and finite-element simulations. Transport measurements further reveal a strong dependence of transition characteristics - and even the occurrence of superconductivity itself - on average terrace width. These results identify step-induced weak links as the microscopic origin of two-step transitions in bilayer nickelate films, providing a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative transport, and a route to superconducting devices.
summary: This work investigates the origin of two-step superconducting transitions in bilayer nickelate films. The authors demonstrate that these transitions are caused by superconducting weak links formed at the substrate step-terrace boundaries. By combining transport measurements with structural modeling, they establish a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative superconductivity in these complex materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the physical origin of the characteristic two-step superconducting transition observed in bilayer nickelate thin films.
main_result: The two-step transition is identified as arising from superconducting weak links located at the substrate step-terrace structures, which governs anisotropic and percolative transport.
method: The study combines transport measurements (resistive measurements, azimuthal dependence) with structural characterization (AFM, STEM) and theoretical modeling (simple models, finite-element simulations).
model_or_system: The system is bilayer nickelate thin films grown on SrLaAlO4 substrates. The physics is modeled by treating the film as a composite of pristine superconducting regions (high Tc) and weak-link regions at the steps (low Tc).
key_observables: Two-step superconducting transitions in resistivity vs. temperature ($ho(T)$), anisotropy in transition behavior based on current direction, and dependence of zero resistance on average terrace width.
important_parameters: Superconducting transition temperatures ($T_c$), coherence length ($\xi_{ab}$), weak-link barrier thickness ($L_{	ext{strain}}$), and average step-terrace width.
main_assumptions: The superconducting behavior can be modeled by considering the film as a percolation network of two distinct superconducting regions (pristine vs. weak-link).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-step transitions under varying current directions relative to step-terrace orientation, and simulations/models reproduce the observed anisotropy and dependence on the relative area of the weak-link region.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental observation of two-step transitions, correlates this anisotropy with the step-terrace geometry, develops a two-region model (pristine/weak-link), and validates this model using finite-element simulations and by showing dependence on terrace width.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how structural disorder (steps) can induce mesoscopic superconducting behavior, which relates to understanding phase coherence and transport in complex, disordered superconducting materials.
